speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked	the Prime Minister (a) over the past two terms of Parliament, how many times has the Presidential Council for Minority Rights suggested changes to, or withheld assent to, a Bill passed in Parliament; (b) when have these actions taken place; and (c) over what issues have the Council proposed changes or withheld its assent.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Second, the Member should be aware that the Council's opinion is publicly available.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Since Independence, the PAP Government has made equality of races and religions fundamental to its vision of a multi-racial, multi-religious Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Therefore, it is most unlikely that any legislation from the Government will disadvantage any racial or religious group and cause the Council to raise any objection.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Nevertheless, the PAP Government created the PCMR as a unique institution that will help to protect the rights of minorities and reassure minority communities of their place in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The PCMR, as an institution and process, is valuable, in case any legislation passed inadvertently disadvantages any party, or there comes a day when a different government in Singapore operates on a different basis.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In addition, before a Bill is introduced in Parliament, it goes through legal and legal policy oversight.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Ministries seek the Attorney-General's Chambers' (AGC) legal advice on the legality of their actions before implementing policies by way of new legislation or legislative amendment.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MinLaw examines draft legislation to ensure that it is consistent with the Constitution and other legal policies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: These include, for instance, whether the Bill might directly or indirectly be disadvantageous to persons from particular racial or religious communities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Former Chief Justice, Mr Chan Sek Keong, now Senior Judge, had previously observed that it is for similar reasons that the volume of judicial review in Singapore is relatively low.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The fact that there has not been any adverse reports bears testament to the robustness of the system of checks that we have and the commitment of the PAP Government to racial and religious equality.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Member would be familiar with the Bills passed in the past few years.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If the Member believes that the PCMR should have drawn attention to a certain Bill, we would be happy to invite him to indicate the Bills which he is referring to.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the Minister be able to share if the PCMR in the past, at anytime in the course of its deliberations, has requested to interview any public servants or experts, or requested any data from the Government in order to assess the economic, social or other impact of any legislation?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But at any one point in time, before the Bill is presented to the PCMR, it would have gone through three layers of checks: the AGC, the MinLaw and Parliament.
